title: Old funerals with horses, white and black coffins, and societies
summary: Ernie describes funerals with horse-drawn hearses, white for the young and black for the old, and slow marches. Society members turned out in blue suits and derbies, with bands and big second lines, no police.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Were they much different in those days than they are now?

Yeah, very much different. I'll tell you why. One reason. It wasn't as fast as they are now. See, in those days, they had horses pulling the horses and carriages in the back. And if it was a young person, 20 years old, you knew it because they had white horses, and they had white mantles on the horses, and they were buried in a white coffin. They didn't have caskets then. And the driver had a white piece of ribbon tied on his whip.

Now, if it was a person over 20 years old, they had a brown or black coffin or gray, and they had black horses with their black mantles on them, and they had a black ribbon tied on every driver. You know, it was someone over 20 years old. Then you used to have the young white galleys, the old white galleys, the artisan society, all those societies. We didn't have all these insurances you have now. And plenty of people belonged to society. Well, they would have to turn out for the funeral, or either have to pay their dollar fine for the people to pay their dollar fine. They all turned out. And all the men in those days wore their blue suits and their black derby. That's right. And the women would walk on the sidewalk, and the men would walk on the street behind the funeral, and the bands would be in between them. Well, the horses would walk so slow, it'd take them about an hour to get out of one block. That's just how slow they would be going, you see. Until the bands stopped playing. Then when they started playing the funeral march, then the horses would walk past them until they stopped. The drum roll, and the horses, the old horses, right.
All the children used to have done this too, you know.

That would give a better chance for the people to come out that wants to see it, and that would make you have a larger second line, more people in the funeral and everything else. But now, they take them out, and before you heard, they're gone.
You know what I don't remember? Maybe you could remember. I don't even remember seeing no policemen out there behind the second lines. No.
I don't even remember seeing no policemen. They didn't have them. That's right. They didn't have them. They didn't have them.
